text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you describe when the swelling and pain in your right ring finger first started and if there was any specific injury or event that triggered it? Also, have you noticed any redness, warmth, or discharge from the area?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you hear or feel a "pop" at the time of injury, and are you currently able to fully extend or flex the finger? I also need to know if there is any visible deformity or if the finger looks crooked compared to the others.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

text: Thank you for the results. Since the X-ray rules out a fracture, I suspect a tendon injury. Can you confirm if the tip of your finger stays straight and you are unable to bend it downwards, even when trying to make a fist? This specific inability to flex the distal joint suggests a flexor tendon issue.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text: Can you confirm if the very tip of your finger remains straight and you are completely unable to bend it downward, even when trying to make a tight fist? This specific inability to flex the distal interphalangeal joint is the hallmark sign of a Jersey Finger injury.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, numbness, or tingling in the affected finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for ruling out nerve involvement. Given the mechanism of injury and your specific inability to flex the distal joint, I am confident in the diagnosis of a flexor digitorum profundus tendon avulsion, commonly known as Jersey Finger. DIAGNOSIS READY: Jersey Finger (Flexor Digitorum Profundus Avulsion)
